claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - my daughter Alex. She's 14 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex. Let me gather a bit more detail to assess your eligibility properly.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't actually live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Living abroad can affect Child Benefit eligibility, so this is important information.

**Are you a Crown servant (such as someone working for the UK government abroad), or do you live in one of the countries where you can still claim Child Benefit while living abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I'm just living abroad - not working for the UK government.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's helpful to know.

**Which country are you currently living in?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say exactly which country, but it's not one where I'd be eligible to claim UK benefits from abroad. I'm just wondering if there's any way I could still claim for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you being straightforward about that. Based on what you've shared, this is an important point:

According to the Child Benefit rules, you may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant. Since you've indicated that:

1. You're not living in a country where you can claim UK Child Benefit from abroad
2. You're not a Crown servant

Unfortunately, this means you would not qualify for Child Benefit under the standard eligibility rules, as you're not living in the UK.

However, I want to make sure I have the complete picture before making a final determination. Let me ask one more question:

**Is there any possibility that Alex is currently living with someone else in the UK (such as a family member or guardian), rather than living with you abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is living here with me abroad. She's not in the UK with anyone else.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

Based on the information you've provided, I can now make my determination:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

The key issue is that Child Benefit requires you to live in the UK. While Alex meets the age requirement (being 14 years old and under 16), and you are clearly responsible for her, the UK residency requirement is a fundamental part of the eligibility criteria.

The only exceptions to this are if you:
- Live in certain specific countries where UK benefits can be claimed from abroad, or
- Are a Crown servant working abroad

Since neither of these applies to your situation, unfortunately you don't qualify for Child Benefit at present.

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you return to the UK or if you move to one of the countries where Child Benefit can be claimed—you may be able to claim then. You can find more information by contacting HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) Child Benefit Office if you'd like to explore your specific situation further.
